summary: Physical active support has ruḥo as a reflexive object (91/16; 52/36) or beams as an ordinary object with -nne (MAC Ishaq old houses/53). The social l- patron frame specializes the reflexive construction in 1b.

91/16 does not directly show b- introducing the support: b u ṭurawo names the mountain; the sticks are supplied as an antecedent. Do not derive a physical-versus-social b-/l- alternation from the translation alone.
Detransitive snido is a supported/leaning state, while dməsnodi ləḥḏoḏe is reciprocal material support. Neither requires an agentive reading.
Existing examples at 52/36 and 91/16 are not re-added, and the matching stone-support clause is identified by citation correction rather than another quotation.
Round 1 already added Infectum-wa. sundiwonne and səndowale fill that still-thin cell rather than establishing it again.

The navel has a feminine patient suffix with b mede as supporting means. In ksundile, an understood plural supporter has a singular person patient. In səndowale, Maḥbe is the feminine supporter and the Xori the helped person; b answers expresses the means/domain.
The social-help tokens lack the ruḥo plus l-patron frame required by round-1 1b. Retain ordinary sense 1 rather than assigning every social use to that subsense.
Does snədde ruḥayye lann aġawiye at JTM 3.3/12 imply protection, patronage, submission, or simply securing support? The proposed gloss deliberately avoids formal subordination.
Confirm the legacy MlfI_Houses2/73 numbering against the supplied MAC Ishaq Material culture/70 reference; both markers are preserved.

Jan 2.33/5391: the isolated verse says women’s work but does not explicitly name childbirth or the helped people. Verify the wider situation before using the reader’s support women in labour as a specialized sense.
Jan 3.5/64: confirm the referent and relationship denoted by i baṯ-qyomo Maḥbe; the supplied machine English wife is not independent lexical evidence.
Support applies to a bodily part, an enlightened person, and an interviewee helped by suggested answers. Physical support and helping are already in the inherited gloss; none requires a new sense.
